full_judgment:
Hence, I am to see whether the left out co sharers are necessary parties in this suit for declaration and permanent injunction. As per the averments of the plaint all the co-sharers including the left out co-sharers have subsisting interest in the property. If for any reason the plaintiffs could not implead Himangshu and Arunangshu in the category of plaintiffs. I cannot understand why the plaintiffs could not implead these co-sharers as defendants when the objection was raised at the earliest point of time by the contesting defendants. In this suit it is not possible to split up the joint interest of the parties in the land. It is further found that the plaintiffs are not suing in their personal capacity but suing as co-sharers in possession of the suit land. It is quite clear that the plaintiffs filed the suit on specific averments of joint interest in an unpartitioned land and having sued in that capacity all must be brought on record. It cannot be said that the left out co-sharers are not jointly interested in the immovable property and that being the position they must be brought on record as they have direct interest in the suit property. In a suit for declaration and permanent injunction if the plaintiffs get a decree then the same conclusively binds all the parties and in that event it is undisputed that the suit ought to have been heard in presence of all the co-sharers for an effective decree within the frame of the suit. The main averments is that, all the co-sharers are interested in all the lands but the plaintiffs are in possession as co-owners and in that view a cosharer in possession is certainly entitled under the law to maintain a suit for declaration and permanent injunction to protect his proprietary right in it but all joint owners must be on record for proper constitution of the suit as they are jointly interested in the subject matter of the suit. Thus, I find that the plaintiffs suit is in fact defective for want of necessary parties and it cannot proceed. This being a case of declaration of title and permanent injunction the plaintiff is oblige to make out a case of good title for all the co-sharers and this issue of title could not be decided leaving these two admitted co-sharers. Section 53 of the Specific Relief Act says that a decree for permanent injunction can only be granted upon the merits of the suit. The plaintiffs story of amicable partition of "B' schedule properties and acquisition of absolute ownership by the plaintiffs was not accepted by the courts below. Further, the division of 'A' schedule properties by metes and bounds was also not accepted by the courts below. Hence, right, title and interest cannot be finally concluded without the necessary parties. In a suit for declaration and perpetual injunction the plaintiff must first establish his legal right. After the plaintiff succeeds in establishing his legal right and its violation he is granted a permanent injunction. Permanent injunction can be granted by the decree made at the hearing and upon the merits of a suit which concludes a right for ever. Thus, unless the rights of all persons who have joint right, title and interest are brought on record, no violation of right of all persons can be determined. Thus it is very simple that all joint owners must be on record. Where there is a joint right it may be necessary for all persons jointly interested to be joined as parties, and if they are not joined the suit will be bad for misjoinder. The immovable property being jointly owned each co-owner is in theory Interested in every portion of the suit land and each has a right, irrespective of the quantity of his share. Due to the conflicting averments and adverse claim which was not accepted by the courts blow, the co-owners ought to have been made parties. In paragraph 16 of the plaint it has been stated that all the co-sharers have been made proforma defendants. This factual assertion is also not correct as admittedly two of the co-sharers are left out. Further, there is averments that if any of the proforma defendant contests the suit he may be treated as a principal defendant. Hence it is palpable to say that the plaintiffs have got no consent to file the suit on behalf of these left out co sharers and that their interest is also adverse to be plaintiffs interest. From the very beginning of the suit the objection as to non-joinder of necessary parties was raised specifically in the written statement, even then the plaintiff did not care to implead these two admitted co-sharers namely. Himangshu and Arunangshu as parties. This is one of the circumstances also which lends support to the fact that the plaintiffs are claiming as if they are only heirs of Harimohan Paul. 

 "It is true that under O. 1, R. 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure no suit shall be defeated by reason of the misjoinder or non-joinder of the parties, but there can be no doubt that if the parties who are not joined are not only proper but also necessary parties to it, the infirmity in the suit is bound to be fatal. Even in such cases; the Court can under O. 1, R. 10, sub-rule 2 direct the necessary parties to be joined, but all this can and should be done at the stage of trial and that too without prejudice to the said parties plea of limitation.
